criteria.reasoning: The memo computes "Adjusted program expenses $4,886,000" ($19,066,000 less $14,180,000) over "Adjusted total functional expenses $6,240,000" ($20,515,000 less "all gifts in kind expensed" $14,275,000). Depreciation is kept in: "Depreciation remains included because the policy does not exclude it."
The memo reports "$4,886,000 ÷ $6,240,000 × 100 = 78.3%" as the program expense ratio, and the summary table also shows 78.3%.
The memo says "The 80.0% minimum was not met; the result is 1.7 percentage points below target", and the table marks it "Not met". Every statement in the memo is consistent on this point.

The memo does remove the bequest ("Less: bequest received in 2025 ($600,000) | Audit Note 10") and names it as the Okafor estate distribution. It never says why, though: there is no statement that the policy excludes bequests or estate distributions, or that they are non-recurring. The only explanation is "The excluded bequest was the unrestricted $600,000 distribution from the Estate of Harriet M. Okafor." The criterion requires the reason to be given.
The memo shows "Adjusted contributions $3,985,000" ($18,930,000 less $14,345,000 noncash less the $600,000 bequest).
The memo reports "$866,300 ÷ $3,985,000 = $0.22 per dollar raised".

The memo says "The $0.20 maximum was not met" and that management must present corrective plans for "both the program expense ratio and the cost to raise a dollar". The opening summary's "two of the three targets were met" implies otherwise, but the memo itself retracts it: "Correction to the summary assessment: One of the three targets was met." The table, the section and the follow-up all say not met, so the memo's final position on this target is consistent.
The reserve starts from "Net assets without donor restrictions, year-end $6,612,000", and the memo states "The $1,240,000 of donor-restricted net assets is excluded."
The memo computes "Operating reserve $1,504,000" ($6,612,000 less $5,108,000 land, buildings and equipment, net).
The memo's "Annual operating expenses $5,794,000" is $20,515,000 less $446,000 depreciation less $14,275,000 of gifts in kind expensed.
The memo says "The 3.0-month minimum was met", and the table marks the reserve "Met".

Every figure traces to the files or is computed from them: the Note 9 gifts in kind ($14,345,000 received, $14,275,000 expensed, the $70,000 inventory difference), the Part VIII/IX/X lines, the Note 10 bequest, and the April 22, 2026 audit and August 11, 2026 filing dates. The memo introduces no prior-year ratio, budget or benchmark. Its wrong "two of the three targets" summary is a misstatement judged by other criteria, not an unsupported figure.
